title: Unidentified correspondence-course fees decision — assigned account, identity unresolved
citation: Unidentified Cour de cassation decision; assigned printed p. 200 (physical p. 115)
lead: A student leaves a distance course after nine months, and the assigned account reports that the institution’s claim for the remaining installments succeeds in cassation.

actors.name: The student
actors.role: Unnamed customer contracting for six years of distance classes.

actors.name: The institution
actors.role: Unnamed provider seeking the remaining agreed fee installments.

proceedings: The assigned account reports that a lower court refused the remaining fees.
It reports that the Court of Cassation quashed that refusal; the case identity and complete order remain unresolved.
limits: Only the assigned paragraph is available. There is no verified caption, date, docket, actual judgment, complete reasoning or remand detail. The nearby July 9, 2003 citation concerns a dental-practice dispute and does not identify this student case.

review.basis: Individually written and compared with the canonical full brief; no new independent opinion audit claimed.

sections.title: A student agrees to a long course with installments
sections.cue: What service and payment schedule does the assignment describe?
paragraphs: The assigned chapter describes an unnamed student’s contract with an unnamed institution for distance classes over six years. The stated payment arrangement was a thirty-franc enrollment charge followed by thirty-five monthly installments of forty francs.

The six-year service period and the thirty-five-payment schedule are separate features of the reported agreement. The chapter provides no case-specific caption, judgment date or docket identifying the parties’ litigation.

sources.pinpoint: Contract and source status; assigned p. 200

sections.title: The student seeks to leave after nine months
sections.cue: What balance does the institution demand?
paragraphs: Nine months after the course began, the student sought to terminate the arrangement. The institution demanded the remaining twenty-six monthly installments.

The account does not state why he withdrew, whether further instruction continued or was tendered, or what termination terms the contract contained. It describes a demand for the unpaid agreed installments, not twenty-six years of tuition or a newly calculated additional damages claim.

sources.pinpoint: Contract and dispute reported; assigned p. 200

sections.title: The lower court refuses to order payment
sections.cue: What judicial step precedes cassation in the reported account?
paragraphs: The chapter reports that the lower court refused to order payment of the remaining fees. It does not supply that court’s full reasoning or the student’s pleaded defenses.

The institution’s claim thus reached the Court of Cassation after an adverse ruling on the fee balance. The unavailable details do not establish a statutory basis or an additional ruling on the parties’ other obligations.

sections.title: The reported refusal is quashed, but the complete order is missing
sections.cue: What does the assigned illustration establish?
paragraphs: The chapter says the Court of Cassation quashed the refusal and held that the institution could recover the entire fee balance. It presents the case as an illustration of a creditor seeking the agreed contract price, as distinct from substitute damages or termination.

The exact order, remand court, costs, judicial author and votes remain unknown. Nearby discussion of later grace-period provisions and the 2016 reforms supplies no basis to attribute those rules to this unidentified decision.

sources.pinpoint: Reported result and assigned limits; assigned p. 200 & nn. 29–33
